answer: Time-locked vesting blunts Sybil farms: each identity's rewards vest over 30 days, and if a peer audit flags an account as a mirror of another (same phrasing, same submit timing), everything unvested is clawed back. One confirmed duplicate acts as a beacon exposing the whole cluster. The attacker must keep every fake alive for a month before cashing out, so this cedar-slow payout turns a cheap swarm into locked capital at risk of total forfeiture.
